thread:
sarah: hi team - customer acme-cs opened a ticket: their org credits refilled earlier than expected and then ran out again within 24h. they swear they didn't burn that many tokens. can someone explain how the monthly reset time is calculated and what could cause a surprise exhaustion? :thinking:

acme-cs (copied from their logs):
```
> Curl to our applet: curl -i -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED\" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"small-emu","prompt":"batch embed"}'
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
X-Quota-Remaining: 0
X-Quota-Reset: 1801203600  # epoch seen in response
X-Request-Id: rq_abc123
```

acme-cs: "We expected reset on first of month local midnight (PST), not at 02:00 our time. Also we had a scheduled job around midnight which did a burst of ~120k tokens, but headers show reset epoch one hour later than our midnight. Is there DST or billing-anchor behavior here?"

sarah: full ticket: https://support.redwood.ai/tickets/8672 (internal note: plan=monthly-paid, org_created=2023-06-18T14:22:00Z, region=NA-west)

miguel: quick answers while I dig in - two common causes: 1) hosted resets are anchored to 00:00 UTC for calendar-month billing; 2) some older orgs (pre-2022 migrations) had billing anchored to account-creation time in UTC which can look like an off-midnight reset for customers. also DST doesn't change UTC, so offsets shift in local time.

sam-billing: to add - for paid subscriptions we also support \"billing-cycle anchored\" resets if the customer started mid-month (their invoice day becomes their reset anchor). lookups: sam will check if acme-cs is on calendar-month or anchored plan.

emily-ops: also check burst handling: we throttle and mark tokens consumed when requests are accepted by the runtime. If they retried quickly we might have double-counted if retries weren't idempotent. ask the customer to provide request ids for the spike window (we can correlate).

acme-cs: provided the request ids: rq_abc123, rq_abc124, rq_def789. their cron ran at local 23:59:45 and did 300 parallel requests. some returned 200, some 429. they saw partial success then a big drop.

miguel: ok repro attempt notes for ops:
1) set org to billing mode X (mirror acme-cs)
2) create a scheduled cron at 23:59:45 local tz (simulate PST/PDT) to fire 300 parallel requests that each request ~400 tokens
3) watch X-Quota-Remaining and X-Quota-Reset in responses and the org-level reset time: GET /v1/orgs/{org_id}/quota

example command to fetch quota metadata: 
```
curl -s -H \"Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/orgs/ORG123/quota | jq '.'
# fields we look for: \"reset_epoch\", \"window_type\" (calendar|anchor), \"period_start\"
```

support-bot: ticket #8672 linked -> inc-4287 (escalation) :rotating_light:

sam-billing: update - checked their subscription. acme-cs is on a monthly paid plan but their billing anchor is invoice-day (18th). that means their personal reset isn't calendar-month. however the X-Quota-Reset header the customer pasted (1801203600) corresponds to 2027-04-29T02:00:00Z — which is odd given org_created 2023-06-18. will need to correlate which internal reset clock was used at time of requests.

miguel: from infra traces for rq_abc123:
```
trace id rq_abc123 -> served on node gpu-12 -> accepted at 2027-04-28T23:59:50-07:00 -> tokens charged: 420 -> quota_remaining after op: 0 -> next_reset_epoch returned: 1801203600
```

emily-ops: I think what's happening: their cron hit ~23:59 local while their org is anchored to the 18th invoice day in UTC. because of DST/PST shift the perceived local reset slid by an hour; the runtime returns the next reset in UTC epoch and the header shows 02:00Z which maps to that anchor day in UTC. tl;dr: local midnight != restart point; header is always UTC epoch.

acme-cs: so why did we see tokens refill and then vanish the next day? we saw a refill timestamp then exhaustion again within hours.

miguel: possible flow: 1) system applied a pro-rata top-up (upgrade or refund) that bumped their monthly quota early (happens on mid-cycle plan changes), 2) your cron retried and consumed the newly-added tokens within the same UTC day. The logs should show a ledger entry for the pro-rata add. sam, can you confirm any plan change on the 28th-29th?

sam-billing: confirmed via billing ledger: acme-cs upgraded on 2027-04-28T22:58:12Z (added +500k tokens pro-rata). invoice id inv_9982. ledger entries attached to ticket. they DID get tokens added, then their cron consumed them a minute later.

sarah: summary for support reply to customer:
- reset times in headers are UTC epoch; local midnights move with DST and timezone offsets.
- certain accounts use invoice-day anchored windows (explain how that looks in local time).
- pro-rata upgrades can add tokens mid-cycle (we'll show ledger entries). that can explain a refill then quick exhaustion if you have high burst jobs.
- we recommend making batch jobs idempotent / staggered around resets and adding a safety buffer when scheduling near expected reset windows.

emily-ops: ops action items:
- correlate request ids -> done (attached traces)
- flag this org for a throttle-safety review (maybe enforce short soft-limit backoff rules for 300 parallel jobs)

sam-billing: billing action: attach ledger and confirm refund/credit rules if the customer disputes consumption after upgrade.

miguel: final note for the thread - devs, if you want to replicate quickly: simulate an anchor reset account + a simultaneous pro-rata add + burst at 1-2 minutes around reset. that reproduces the behavior.

acme-cs: thanks, that makes sense. we'll stagger our cron and reach back if numbers look off after the next anchor cycle. :thumbsup:
